title: data import: POST /api/v1/data/:object/import reports an undeclared hook refusal as row code IMPORT_ROW_FAILED, while every other write door answers HOOK_ABORTED
body:
domain:server#6 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzibcN9oHa8kDbTTnL5

Filing gate: ① a product defect with a named landing point. Found by the #29894 dev's sweep (PR #29977) and measured live on a dogfood boot.
Business reason: #27597 gave an undeclared hook `onError` abort one wire code, `HOOK_ABORTED`, so a client can tell "a business rule refused this row" from "the input is malformed" and show the hook's sentence. After PR #29977, `/data`, `/createMany`, `/batch` and every `/data/:object/batch` row answer it. The import door's row still answers `IMPORT_ROW_FAILED` for the same abort, so an import client that branches on the code cannot tell a hook refusal from any other row failure. Import is where bulk business data comes in.
Reader who acts: `domain:server`. The landing point is the core import runner's `toFailedResult` (a different mapper from `toRowApiError` in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-client-failures.ts`, which PR #29977 fixed).
Dedupe (open and closed): `IMPORT_ROW_FAILED HOOK_ABORTED`. The nearest are #29894 (the batch row, landing in PR #29977) and #27597 (closed, the doors it moved).

## What to fix

- An import row whose failure is a sandboxed hook abort with no declared code answers `HOOK_ABORTED` with the hook's sentence, by the same predicate `toRowApiError` now uses (`isUndeclaredHookAbort` / `UNDECLARED_HOOK_REFUSAL_CODE`). Reuse it rather than writing a second judge. A declared code still wins. Other import row failures keep `IMPORT_ROW_FAILED`, unless the import contract says otherwise: measure what the import result's row code vocabulary promises before changing it.
- Pin: the #29894 dogfood fixture (an object whose `beforeInsert` throws a free-text error) through `/data/:object/import`, beside the batch-row pin.
